chapter: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
title: Joe Steele's band and Boston working musicians
summary: He met Joe Steele in church; Hodges and Howard Johnson worked with Steele's band, and Carney worked a road house for nearly a year.

story.theme_name: First paying gigs: getting started as a young professional
story.community_name: First paid gigs: pay, bands and young beginnings

blocks.x: Did you meet Joe Steele(?) here?

No. I met Joe Steele in church. His sister was my Sunday School teacher. I was going to Sunday School in them days, as a little boy. His mother... They were very religious people. Yeah, I met Joe in church.
Did you do any gigging with Joe Steele?

Not up there. He had his own band up there. Good band, too. Yeah, very good. He was a pretty big name, drawing, you know. Nothing like bands draw today, I mean, but at that time... And I didn't work with him. Let me see... Johnny worked with him. Johnny was with Joe's band. And Howard worked with him quite a bit -- Howard Johnson. But Howard did a lot of steady work in Boston, at different clubs and things. He would work there for year-in and year-out, you know, be there quite a while.

In fact, Harry Carney, he worked in a road house quite a while... Actually quite a while, because I think we only had our saxophones about a year or so before both of us come to New York. But up until then, he had been working this road house -- Harry Carney. He had been working there almost a year.
